headline_marked: Woman's [[dismembered body found in suitcase]] under Gazipur culvert
headline: Woman's dismembered body found in suitcase under Gazipur culvert
summary: Police recovered the decomposed remains of an unidentified woman, aged 30-35, from a suitcase and sacks under a culvert near the Dhaka-Mymensingh highway.
details: Police in Gazipur's Joydebpur have recovered the dismembered and decomposed remains of an unidentified woman from under a culvert near the Dhaka-Mymensingh highway.
Local residents discovered a blue suitcase under a culvert in the Bhavani-pur area of Joydebpur, near Fikira Garments, on Friday afternoon.
Upon opening the suitcase, police found parts of a woman's body. Further searches in the surrounding area led to the recovery of other body parts stored in sacks.
The recovered remains were sent to the Gazipur Shaheed Tajuddin Ahmad Medical College morgue for an autopsy to determine the cause of death.
Joydebpur Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Al Mamun stated that the woman is estimated to be between 30 and 35 years old.
Police are currently collecting evidence from the scene and working to identify the victim and investigate the cause of her death.
Preliminary suspicions suggest the woman may have been killed elsewhere and her body was subsequently dismembered and dumped in the suitcase and sacks at the location.
caption:
A blue suitcase found under a culvert in Gazipur revealed a horrific discovery: the dismembered remains of a woman.

Police in Gazipur's Joydebpur have recovered the dismembered and decomposed remains of an unidentified woman from under a culvert near the Dhaka-Mymensingh highway.

Local residents discovered a blue suitcase under a culvert in the Bhavani-pur area of Joydebpur, near Fikira Garments, on Friday afternoon.

Upon opening the suitcase, police found parts of a woman's body. Further searches in the surrounding area led to the recovery of other body parts stored in sacks.

The recovered remains were sent to the Gazipur Shaheed Tajuddin Ahmad Medical College morgue for an autopsy to determine the cause of death.

Joydebpur Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Al Mamun stated that the woman is estimated to be between 30 and 35 years old.

Police are currently collecting evidence from the scene and working to identify the victim and investigate the cause of her death.

Preliminary suspicions suggest the woman may have been killed elsewhere and her body was subsequently dismembered and dumped in the suitcase and sacks at the location.

headline_marked: Journalist [[Pulak Chatterjee found dead]] at Samakal bureau office
headline: Journalist Pulak Chatterjee found dead at Samakal bureau office
summary: The former Barishal Press Club general secretary left five notes citing distress over illness and unemployment.
details: Pulak Chatterjee, a former bureau chief of Samakal and former general secretary of the Barishal Press Club, was found dead at the newspaper's Barishal bureau office on Friday.
Police recovered five notes from the scene, which indicated that Pulak had been struggling with prolonged illness and unemployment.
In one note, he mentioned that he had sought treatment in Vellore, India, but his condition did not improve, stating he could no longer bear the suffering.
A heartbreaking message to his daughter, Prakritee, included an apology and a request for her to continue her studies and music lessons.
He also urged his daughter to stay with her uncle, Deepak, and wrote, "Forgive me – no one can wait forever for another person in this world."
Barishal Metropolitan Police Commissioner Abu Raihan Muhammad Saleh stated that based on the notes and circumstances, police believe it was a case of suicide.
Pulak's brother, Deepak Lal Chatterjee, said Pulak had left home around 3:00pm that day, telling his family he was going to get his clothes ironed.
The body was taken to Sher-e-Bangla Medical College Hospital for an autopsy, despite a request in one of the notes to skip the procedure.
caption:
Five heartbreaking notes left behind. A journalist's struggle with illness and unemployment ends in tragedy.

Pulak Chatterjee, a former bureau chief of Samakal and former general secretary of the Barishal Press Club, was found dead at the newspaper's Barishal bureau office on Friday.

Police recovered five notes from the scene, which indicated that Pulak had been struggling with prolonged illness and unemployment.

In one note, he mentioned that he had sought treatment in Vellore, India, but his condition did not improve, stating he could no longer bear the suffering.

A heartbreaking message to his daughter, Prakritee, included an apology and a request for her to continue her studies and music lessons.

He also urged his daughter to stay with her uncle, Deepak, and wrote, "Forgive me – no one can wait forever for another person in this world."

Barishal Metropolitan Police Commissioner Abu Raihan Muhammad Saleh stated that based on the notes and circumstances, police believe it was a case of suicide.

Pulak's brother, Deepak Lal Chatterjee, said Pulak had left home around 3:00pm that day, telling his family he was going to get his clothes ironed.

The body was taken to Sher-e-Bangla Medical College Hospital for an autopsy, despite a request in one of the notes to skip the procedure.
